headline: Approved five policy revisions including BGAA, JFABD, ACA renaming, new ACA discrimination policy, and AC-R2 for recommendation to full board.
summary: The Policy Committee reviewed and approved several school district policies, including BGAA on policy development, JFABD on homeless and unaccompanied youth admissions, and updates to ACA and AC-R policies covering transgender staff protections and discrimination/harassment procedures. Two additional policies, EHB on data records retention and DAF on federal grant fund administration, were discussed and moved for approval, but the minutes do not record a final vote count for these two items.
decisions: Approved policy BGAA, Policy Development, Adoption, and Review, to move to the full board, 2-0.
Approved policy JFABD, Admission of Homeless Children and Unaccompanied Youth, without change, to move to the full board, 2-0.
Approved renaming policy ACA to AC-R1, Transgender and Non-Conforming Staff, with no changes, to move to the full board, 3-0.
Approved new policy ACA, Discrimination and Harassment: Policy and Grievance Procedure, to move to the full board, 3-0.
Approved renaming policy AC-R to AC-R2, Sexual Discrimination Appendix, to move to the full board, 3-0.

Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve ACA Discrimination and Harassment: Policy and Grievance Procedure and move to the full board. Motion passes 3-0.

POLICY COMMITTEE MEETING 
TUESDAY, AUGUST 18, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Policy Committee was held at NHS North on Tuesday, August 18, 2026.   
Ms. Raymond called the meeting to order at 6:03 pm.  
 
Present: Ms. Raymond, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Lamphier (6:13 pm) 
 
Also Present: Mr. O’Rourke and Dr. Andrade 
 
Also Present: Members of the Public, Channel 22 Videographer 
 
 
Policy BGAA - Policy Development, Adoption, and Review  
• Mr. O'Rourke and Ms. Raymond discuss the complementary nature of BDFA (NHSBA) and BGAA 
(Nashua) regarding policy development. 
• Mr. Johnson confirms there were no edits to the BGAA policy. 
• Mr. O'Rourke explains the committee's decision to bring BGAA back for approval after reviewing other 
districts' policies. 
• Ms. Raymond notes that the school board association's BDFA policy is not being adopted as 
components were already covered by Nashua policy BGAA which was dovetailed to the District. 
• Mr. Johnson and Ms. Raymond agree to approve BGAA as it is. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve policy BGAA Policy Development, Adoption, and 
Review and move to the full board. Motion passes 2-0. 
 
Policy JFABD  
• Ms. Raymond introduces JFABD, a policy on the admission of homeless children and unaccompanied 
youth. 
• The policy had recommended changes from NHSBA, however, the Nashua policy had already 
implemented the changes in a previous review cycle. 
• It is the recommendation to approve without additional change. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve policy JFABD Admission of Homeless Children 
and Unaccompanied Youth as reviewed without change and move to the full board. Motion passes 2-0. 
 
Policy ACA (AC-R1) 
• Ms. Raymond introduces Nashua’s current policy titled ACA, Transgender and Non-Conforming Staff 
with the recommendation to re-designate to AC-R1. 
• The NHSBA is recommending a policy entitled ACA which it covers different subject matter.   
• To alleviate confusion, Nashua’s current ACA will be renamed AC-R1, our current policy AC-R will be 
renamed AC-R2.  This will allow for the new discrimination policy to be rightly designated ACA. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to rename policy ACA to AC-R1 Transgender and Non-
Conforming Staff with no changes and move to the full board. Motion passes 3-0. 
 
• Ms. Raymond introduces the new policy titled ACA, covering discrimination, harassment, and 
grievance procedures. 
• The policy includes changes recommended by the civil rights coordinator, such as title changes to match 
district staff. 
• Ms. Raymond explains the policy's purpose and its application to both staff and students. 
• Ms. Lamphier raises questions about the roles of the Title IX coordinator and civil rights compliance 
coordinator.
POLICY COMMITTEE MEETING  AUGUST 18, 2026 
 
2 
• Dr. Andrade explains the roles of the Title IX coordinator and civil rights compliance coordinator. 
• Ms. Raymond and Dr. Andrade discuss the process for handling complaints and grievances. 
• Mr. Johnson suggests changing "school board chair" to "president of the board of education" for 
consistency. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve ACA Discrimination and Harassment: Policy 
and Grievance Procedure and move to the full board. Motion passes 3-0. 
 
Policy AC-R 
• Ms. Raymond proposes renaming the current AC-R policy to AC-R2 and adding the civil rights 
compliance coordinator's contact information. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve policy AC-R to rename as AC-R2 Sexual 
Discrimination Appendix and move to the full board. Motion passes 3-0. 
 
Policy EHB 
• Ms. Raymond introduces the data retention policy, noting no changes since the last update. 
• Mr. O'Rourke explains the policy's purpose and the process for destroying special education records 
upon request. 
• Ms. Raymond and Mr. O'Rourke discuss the implications of destroying special education records and 
the availability of transcripts. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve policy EHB Data Records Retention as reviewed 
without change and move to the full board. 
 
Policy DAF 
• Ms. Raymond introduces the extensive DAF policy on the administration of federal grant funds. 
• Mr. O'Rourke explains the changes, including increased limits for district operations and new sections 
on subrecipient monitoring. 
• The committee discussed the differences between subrecipients and contractors. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve policy DAF Administration of Federal Grant 
Funds and move to the full board. 
 
Future Plans 
• Ms. Raymond reminds the committee of upcoming events, including a public hearing on policy 
regarding video monitoring of school buses and Nashua Goes Back to School night. 
 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to adjourn at 6:52 pm.  Motion passes 3-0.  
 
 
 
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
